spans.s: दिक्क m. A young elephant twenty years old.
दिगीश m. the regent of a quarter, K.S.v.53. (See आशापाल and अष्टदिक्पाल.)
दिगीश m. the regent of a quarter, K.S.v.53. (See आशापाल and अष्टदिक्पाल.)
दिक्कर m. 1. a youth, a youthful man; 2. an epithet of Śiva.
दिक्करिन् m. any of the eight elephants who are said to preside over the eight quarters. (See अष्टदिग्गज.)
दिक्चक्र n. 1. the horizon; 2. the whole world.
दीक्ष् vt. 1Ā (pp. दीक्षित; pres. दीक्षते) 1. To consecrate anyone for the performance of a sacred rite; 2. to dedicate oneself to; 3. to initiate a pupil; 4. to invest with the sacred thread.
दीक्षा f. 1. Consecration for a religious ceremony, R.iii.44, 65; 2. a ceremony preliminary to a sacrifice; 3. investiture with the sacred thread; 4. a ceremony in general, R.iii.33, K.S.viii.24.
दीक्षा-अंत m. a supplementary sacrifice performed to atone the defects in a preceding one.
दीक्षित (I) a. (f. ता) 1. Initiated, consecrated; 2. prepared for a sacrifice, R.viii.75; 3. prepared for, R.iv.5, (pp. of दीक्ष् q.v.).
दीक्षित (II) m. 1. A priest engaged in a dīkshā; 2. a pupil; 3. an appellation affixed to the name of a person who or whose ancestors may have performed the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice.
दीक्षित (I) a. (f. ता) 1. Initiated, consecrated; 2. prepared for a sacrifice, R.viii.75; 3. prepared for, R.iv.5, (pp. of दीक्ष् q.v.).
